title: Identity and Access Management

header.html: 4.5 Given a scenario, apply concepts related to identity and access management
the official CompTIA Security+ SY0-801 V8 exam objectives, document version 2.0

html:
1The identity life cycle

Topic Meaning
Provisioning / deprovisioning Create accounts when people join and remove or disable them when they leave or change roles (prompt deprovisioning prevents stale accounts)
Permissions assignments and implications Grant only what is needed; broad rights raise risk
Identity proofing Verify that a person is who they claim before creating an account
Access review Regularly check who has which rights and remove excess (fights privilege creep)

2Federation and single sign-on

Term Meaning
Federation Trust between organizations so users can use one identity across them
Single sign-on (SSO) Sign in once and reach many applications
SAML XML-based standard to pass authentication between an identity provider and an application (common for web SSO at work)
LDAP Lightweight Directory Access Protocol: query and manage a directory such as Active Directory
OAuth Open standard for authorization: lets one app access another on your behalf without sharing your password
Exam tip

. SAML = authentication across domains (SSO). OAuth = delegated authorization (access to resources). LDAP = directory access. An identity provider (IdP) authenticates; the service provider relies on it.

3Account types

Type Notes
User Normal day-to-day access
Privileged Administrator rights: global (whole environment) or local (one system). Needs extra protection
Service Used by applications and services, not people; avoid interactive sign-in, rotate secrets
Third-party Accounts for vendors or partners: time-limit and monitor
Emergency access (break-glass) Highly privileged, stored securely, used only in emergencies, heavily monitored

4Multifactor authentication (MFA)

MFA combines two or more factors: something you know, have, are, plus (sometimes) where you are or what you do.

Method Meaning
Hard token Physical device (key fob, security key)
Soft token Software on a phone (authenticator app)
Biometrics Fingerprint, face, iris
One-time password (OTP) A code valid once (time-based or counter-based)
Backup code Single-use recovery codes

Exam tip

. A password plus a PIN is not MFA (both are something you know). Password plus a security key is MFA. Store backup codes safely.

5Access control models

Model How access is decided
Discretionary (DAC) The owner decides who gets access
Mandatory (MAC) The system enforces access by labels and clearances (military style)
Role-based (RBAC) By job role
Rule-based By rules (for example firewall rules, "no access from outside the office")
Time-based Allowed only in certain hours
Just-in-time (JIT) Temporary elevated access, only when needed

Access management

Authentication, and policies: logical (technical) such as groups and permissions, and administrative (business) such as hiring and approval rules.

6Password concepts

Topic Notes
Passkey Passwordless sign-in using a cryptographic key pair; resists phishing
Password managers Create and store unique strong passwords
Passwordless Sign in with something other than a password (passkey, biometrics, security key)
Best practices Length (longer is better), complexity, no reuse, expiration and age (modern guidance favors changing only after compromise), compromised credential monitoring, account auditing, policy report
Exam tip

. Length beats complexity. Never reuse passwords. Passkeys are phishing-resistant. Just-in-time access reduces standing privileges.

7Exam Q&A

7.1 Practice questions (choose the best answer)

S1Fabrikam Outdoors wants staff to sign in once and reach many cloud apps using the company identity provider. Which concept fits?

  • AKey escrow
  • BSingle sign-on with federation
  • CHoneypot
  • DPort mirroring
Show the answer

Answer: B. SSO lets users authenticate once, and federation extends the trusted identity to other services.

S2A user must enter a password and then a six-digit code from an authenticator app. Which factors are used?

  • ASomething you know and something you have
  • BSomething you know and something you know
  • CSomething you are and something you do
  • DSomewhere you are and something you know
Show the answer

Answer: A. The password is knowledge and the app code from a phone is a possession factor.

S3A vendor needs administrator rights for two hours to fix a system. Which approach reduces standing privilege?

  • AJust-in-time access
  • BA shared administrator password
  • CPermanent global admin
  • DA service account for the vendor
Show the answer

Answer: A. Just-in-time grants temporary elevated access only when needed.

S4A web app wants to read a user's calendar from another service without getting the user's password. Which standard fits?

  • ALDAP
  • BOAuth
  • CRADIUS
  • DKerberos only
Show the answer

Answer: B. OAuth provides delegated authorization without sharing credentials.

S5After a quarterly review, managers remove access that employees no longer need after moving teams. Which problem is this addressing?

  • APrivilege creep
  • BReplay attacks
  • CKey escrow
  • DTailgating
Show the answer

Answer: A. Access reviews remove accumulated permissions, which is privilege creep.

S6A company sets a rule that a payroll system can only be used from the office between 8 and 6. Which models are combined?

  • ATime-based and rule-based
  • BMandatory and discretionary
  • CRole-based and mandatory
  • DJust-in-time and discretionary
Show the answer

Answer: A. The rule limits by hours (time-based) and by location through rules (rule-based).

7.2 Recall questions

R1What is identity proofing?

Show the answer

Verifying that a person is who they claim to be before creating an account.

R2SAML or OAuth: which is for authentication across domains?

Show the answer

SAML.

R3Name the five account types in the objectives.

Show the answer

User, privileged, service, third-party and emergency access.

R4Name three MFA methods.

Show the answer

For example hard token, soft token, biometrics, one-time password, backup code.

R5What is a passkey?

Show the answer

A passwordless credential based on a cryptographic key pair.

R6Which access control model uses labels and clearances?

Show the answer

Mandatory access control.

8Quick Reference Card

Topic Key fact
Life cycle identity proofing, provisioning, permissions, access reviews, deprovisioning
Federation SSO; SAML (authentication), OAuth (delegated authorization), LDAP (directory)
Accounts user, privileged (global or local), service, third-party, emergency (break-glass)
MFA hard and soft tokens, biometrics, OTP, backup codes; two different factor types
Models DAC, MAC, role-based, rule-based, time-based, just-in-time
Passwords passkeys, password managers, passwordless; length, no reuse, monitor compromised credentials
